compiled_state.title: [merge-to-main-pr.sh _phase_poll]: gh pr checks --json conclusion -> failure detection silently no-ops (pipeline polls until timeout)
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Incident Overview

* **Scenario Type:** User-flagged behavior (37+ min stuck pipeline)
* **code_version:** d3735e7f89a30ca41ebc41f975c3eb5bd4f8df83

### Expected Behavior

When CI checks on the PR enter a terminal failed state (Script Tests FAILURE, llm-review SKIPPED, etc.), `_phase_poll` in plugins/dso/scripts/merge-to-main-pr.sh should detect the failure within one polling interval (~30s) and `return 1`. The downstream `_phase_remediate` then takes over for autonomous CI fix or surfaces to the user.

### Actual Behavior

When PR #255 had Script Tests=FAILURE and llm-review=SKIPPED, the merge-to-main-pr.sh pipeline ran for 37+ minutes without detecting the failure. The user had to manually push a new commit (test fix) to unblock the loop.

### Root Cause Hypothesis

Lines 1538 + 1545-1558 of merge-to-main-pr.sh use:

```
_checks_json=$(gh pr checks "$_pr_number" --json name,state,conclusion 2>&1) || _checks_rc=$?
```

But `gh pr checks --json` only supports the `bucket` field; the requested fields (`name`, `state`, `conclusion`) cause gh to print 'Unknown JSON field: "conclusion"' and exit (in the tested gh version: 0; in others may be non-zero — both paths silently skip failure detection because the python json.load() then fails to parse the error text and the except branch defaults to 'false').

Empirical reproduction:
```
$ gh pr checks 255 --json name,state,conclusion
Unknown JSON field: "conclusion"
Available fields:
  bucket
EXIT=0
```

Result: every poll iteration silently sets `_has_failure="false"` regardless of the actual CI state. The loop only exits when state==MERGED (line 1649) or the timeout fires (line 1680, default 3600s).

### Affected Files

- plugins/dso/scripts/merge-to-main-pr.sh (lines 1538-1558 in _phase_poll; possibly also similar patterns elsewhere)

### Suggested Fix Direction (not prescriptive)

Replace `gh pr checks --json name,state,conclusion` with `gh pr view <PR> --json statusCheckRollup` (which DOES expose state and conclusion per check) and re-derive the FAILURE detection from that. Alternatively, use `gh pr checks --json bucket` and check for `bucket: fail|cancel` values. Add a behavioral test that detects loop hang when a check has FAILURE conclusion.
